record.paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
record.original_question: For an infinite r-regular graph G, let h_G(p) be its p-matching entropy, where p is the limiting density of vertices covered by matchings. Is h_G(p) always at most the p-matching entropy of a countable disjoint union of copies of K_{r,r}, for every p in [0,1]?

evidence.quote: The asymptotic matching conjecture, abbreviated as AUMC, states that G satisfies hG(p) ≤ h∞Kr,r (p) for all p ∈ [0, 1].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $r\ge 1$ be an integer. For a finite graph $H$, a matching of $H$ is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges, and $m_k(H)$ denotes the number of matchings of $H$ with exactly $k$ edges. 

Let $G$ be an infinite, locally finite, $r$-regular graph. Choose any sequence $(G_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of finite induced subgraphs of $G$ whose vertex sets exhaust $V(G)$ and such that the proportion of vertices of $G_n$ that are $r$-regular in $G_n$ tends to $1$. For $p\in[0,1]$, define the $p$-matching entropy of $G$ by
$$h_G(p) \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{|V(G_n)|}\,\log m_{\lfloor p\,|V(G_n)|/2\rfloor}(G_n),$$
assuming the limit exists and is independent of the chosen exhaustion (which is the case under mild homogeneity hypotheses such as $G$ being a Cayley graph or a graph admitting an invariant random regular structure).

Let $K_{r,r}^\infty$ denote the countable disjoint union of copies of the complete bipartite graph $K_{r,r}$, and let $h_{K_{r,r}^\infty}(p)$ be its $p$-matching entropy, defined analogously (which exists and equals $\tfrac{1}{2r}\log m_{\lfloor pr\rfloor}(K_{r,r})$ extended continuously to $p\in[0,1]$).

Prove or disprove: for every infinite $r$-regular graph $G$ (for which $h_G$ is defined) and every $p\in[0,1]$,
$$h_G(p) \;\le\; h_{K_{r,r}^\infty}(p).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The finite Upper Matching Conjecture of Friedland–Krop–Markström, from which the asymptotic version follows, was proved for all sufficiently large $d$-regular bipartite graphs by Davies, Jenssen, Perkins and Roberts (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2021), and Ilinca–Kahn (2013) established asymptotic forms. Earlier, Friedland and collaborators verified the asymptotic matching conjectures in various special cases. The full conjecture for all (not necessarily bipartite, possibly infinite) $r$-regular graphs and all $p\in[0,1]$ does not appear to be completely resolved, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: A proof of the Upper Matching Conjecture for large graphs
status_evidence.snippet: For every d and every large enough n divisible by 2d, a union of n/(2d) copies of K_{d,d} maximizes the number of matchings of size k among all d-regular bipartite graphs on n vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Finite UMC for d-regular bipartite graphs proved for sufficiently large n, implying the asymptotic bipartite version.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics of the Upper Matching Conjecture (Ilinca–Kahn)
status_evidence.snippet: We give upper bounds for the number of matchings of a given size in a regular graph...
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic upper bounds toward the AUMC were established.

status_evidence.title: On the Validations of the Asymptotic Matching Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Validations of asymptotic matching conjectures including the upper matching conjecture for monomer-dimer entropies.
status_evidence.claim: Partial validations of the AUMC have been obtained, indicating the problem is partially resolved.
